title: Punch in on something and hold there
goal: Half of what makes a screen recording watchable is moving the eye: start wide, push in on the thing being talked about, hold, and pull back out. Make that a couple of moves rather than an exercise.
notes:
Build on docs/design/mocks/pages/video-zoom-wt.html, whose whole point is that this is not a special feature: "The move is two keys on Scale and two on Centre, and it is built with the same three gestures as every other animation in Photonz: move the playhead, change the value, and it is recorded."

So this must NOT be a zoom tool. It is the animation model pointed at scale and position. If it needs machinery of its own, the animation model is wrong and that is the finding.

Sharpness is the acceptance item that will actually be hard: a screen recording pushed in on is being magnified past its native resolution, and the app already knows about crisp tiles and nearest-neighbour magnification for exactly this reason. Reuse that thinking.

---
Grounded in the video clickthroughs, which the user says are ideas to build on rather than specs: say in the audit where you went further or differently and why. The thesis every page shares governs this too: video is not a mode, it is the layer document with time.
acceptance: A clip can be pushed in on and pulled back out over time, and the result is smooth rather than stepped
Where it pushes in to is chosen by pointing at the thing on screen, not by typing numbers
It holds where it lands for as long as you want before moving again
It survives a trim: pushing in and then cutting the clip does not leave the move pointing at the wrong place
It stays sharp at the size it ends up: pushing in on a recording does not turn it to mush, and the audit shows the pixels
What plays is what exports, compared frame to frame
Audit under queue/audits/ with a real capture punched in on, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review of the mock, before building. (1) The mock's eight steps are a chore: step 3 keys a value you have not changed, and the mock itself admits it 'feels odd for a second'. A first-time user will not do it, and the acceptance item says where it pushes in to is chosen by POINTING at the thing, not typing numbers. So the gesture is: scrub to the moment, drag a box round the thing, and the camera has arrived on it by that moment. One gesture instead of five. (2) The mock's 'key 100% again wherever you want the move to land' needs a third and fourth key on one property, and the model has exactly two (from and to) with one motion per property. That is the finding the task predicted: a punch in, a hold and a pull back out is a KEY LIST, and the fix belongs in the animation model rather than in a zoom tool. (3) The mock never asks what happens when the clip is cut. A clip's frames slide along the timeline when it is trimmed (ClipPieces lays the pieces back to back), and a motion's clock today is the DOCUMENT's, so a punch in would stay put while the frames it was pointing at moved. A move on a clip belongs to the clip's own clock. (4) Decorative and cut: no separate Reframe effect, no crop mode, no numeric Centre entry as the primary path. (5) The mock's open question about sharpness is answerable rather than a warning: the renderer already keeps the full source frame and scales it into the box, so a 2x recording in a 1x document has headroom, and the app can say how much.

Built. Core: MotionStop (a motion can be nailed to a value part way through, so one property can go out, HOLD and come back, which is what the task predicted would be the finding); Layer.motionClockMS(atDocumentTimeMS:) so a clip's motions are read on the clip's own source clock, which is what makes a punch in survive a trim, a split and a piece being thrown away; ClipReframe.swift, which is arithmetic only — a box on the picture into a Scale percentage and a Position, and the two moves that write them. App: EditorState+Reframe, ReframeInspector (a Reframe section above Motion, readouts not fields), three rows in the Video menu with the mock's own key. Render: a photo drawn bigger than its own pixels now gets the Lanczos resampler in an ordinary composite, not only on a magnified one, which is the sharpness item. 26 new core tests, 8723 tests green, punch-in-and-hold-walk green with 9 real window captures.

Found and fixed by playing it: the first working build tore the canvas in half. Punching in called motionChanged(), which starts the ICON motion preview — its own lap clock — while the transport was still pointing at a frame of the recording, so the canvas was handed two different moments at once. A document that finishes has one clock and it is the playhead's; reframeChanged() stops the preview instead. Visible in the 2026-09-21 17:5x run of the walk and gone in the next one.

left rough: Pull Back Out stays live once the clip is already wide, so a second press writes a leg from 100% to 100% that does nothing visible. Not filed: nothing is lost, nothing reads wrong, and it is one guard when somebody next touches this section. left rough: the Motion rows under Reframe show a punch in as From and To only, so the keys in the middle are not editable there; the strip task filed today is the place that gets fixed. left rough: Scale and Centre are readouts rather than fields, deliberately — pointing at the thing is the gesture and typing a percentage is what it replaces — so there is nowhere to nudge a landing by hand except the Motion rows.

motion-pivot-in-a-corner-walk fails in the motion batch (step 24 expectCue, 'a press here would be none, not grab'). Confirmed pre-existing: already recorded on walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-4 on 2026-09-21 as not caused by the transitions work either. Everything else green: 8 of 9 motion walks, 2 of 2 clip walks, 9 of 9 recording walks, 9 of 9 cut walks.

A clip can be punched in on, held, and pulled back out: drag a box round the thing with M, stand the playhead on the moment, Punch In (Shift Z) and the camera has arrived by that moment; Pull Back Out (Option Shift Z) leaves from the playhead and everything between is a hold nobody asked for. Built as the animation model pointed at Scale and Position, not a zoom tool: the model needed two general additions, a motion that can hold part way through (MotionStop) and a clip's motions read on the clip's own clock so the move survives a trim, a split and a piece thrown away. Sharpness answered with a budget the panel prints rather than a warning, plus the renderer using the good resampler wherever a photo is enlarged past its own pixels (12MP frame at 200% composites in 10ms). Verified: 26 new core tests, 8723 tests green, punch-in-and-hold-walk green with 9 real window captures, and the motion, clip, recording and cut walk batches green apart from motion-pivot-in-a-corner-walk which was already failing and is already filed. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-21-punch-in-and-hold.json with three real screenshots. Commit 46935c65, pushed.
